My true preferences are y > x > z > w. My priority at each school is w: 1, x: 2, y: 1, z: 2. Most applicants favor y > x > w > z.

Let's analyze what happens if I submit my true preferences:

Round 1: I propose to y. Since I have priority 1 at y, I am tentatively accepted.

Since I am tentatively accepted at my most preferred school, y, there's no need to propose anywhere else. I will be matched to y.

Submitting my true preferences leads to my best possible outcome, which is being matched to y. There's no incentive to misrepresent my preferences.

Therefore, submitting my true preference seems like the best strategy. Even if I get rejected from y, I will be accepted at x, which is my second choice.
